brief: Two bases a cell apart, with a drawer that fills the gap between them.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full and piece:2,0,0;full, with the cell at (1,0,0) left empty between them. check_build: no errors, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: A drawer that fills the gap between them
requirements.evidence: The part for this job is the notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf/-fm, also in -x2 double height). It is only offered for an empty spot that touches two bases which also touch each other, on two flats next to each other. With bases on opposite sides of an empty cell (and also with (0,0)+(1,1)), find_sockets offered no notch or bay. The cut-face drawers (long/longbin) were offered only inside a half base's own cell, at (2,0) key w. I tried one and it did not reach into (1,0), so I removed it.

finish.summary: The build has two full bases, at (0,0,0) and (2,0,0), with an empty cell between them. It passes the checks (no errors, mesh clash check clear). I couldn't add a drawer that fills the gap, because the configurator doesn't allow one in this layout. The gap-filling drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch) only fits an empty spot beside two bases that touch each other. For example, with bases at (2,0) and (1,1) it was offered at (2,1) and at (1,0). Two bases on opposite sides of an empty cell get no offer. If you can accept two bases that touch, with the drawer frame filling the spot beside both, I can build that instead. A double-height version is also available.

result.note: No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
